newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada homemaker seeks help from United Nations.
newsitem.headline: Canada homemaker seeks help from United Nations.

text.p: A Canadian woman, frustrated by what she calls Canada's discrimination against stay-at-home mothers, has appealed to the United Nations alleging a violation of human rights.
The United Nations has said it would consider the discrimination complaint.

Beverley Smith, a homemaker and the married mother of four children, said on Thursday she wrote to the United Nations after failing to convince the Canadian government that women working at home should be treated as equals to those in the workforce.
"When I stayed at home with my first child, I noticed I immediately lost social status," Smith, a former teacher, said from her home in this Western Canadian city.
"I couldn't get credit. I couldn't get insurance...I had lost the rights of normal adults in society," Smith said in a telephone interview.

After 20 years of asking the Canadian government to change human rights policies and tax laws regarding homemakers, Smith took her case to the U.N's Division for the Advancement of Women, which responded this month.
The organization has pledged to discuss the matter at a meeting next March. It will also ask Canada to comment on the charges and issue a report in June.
